title: How to tailor a cover letter from your resume and job description
excerpt: Use your resume, target role, and company context to draft a focused letter without starting from a blank page.
author: CareerBOT Team
body: A cover letter that repeats your resume word-for-word wastes the recruiter's time. Its job is to connect specific dots your resume can't: why this role, why this company, and why now.
Start by pulling two or three requirements straight from the job description, then match each one to a real example from your resume. This keeps the letter grounded instead of generic.

Open with a specific hook — a project, a shared value, or a reason you're drawn to the team — rather than a restated job title. Hiring managers read dozens of letters that open the same way; specificity is what gets remembered.
Keep it to three short paragraphs: why you're a fit, one concrete example that proves it, and a clear closing that invites next steps.
Reuse the structure across applications, but change the specifics every time. A letter that could be sent to any company usually reads that way to the person receiving it.
